summary.en: Manipur remains volatile as Kuki-Zo women’s groups and a forum demand President’s Rule and a state MLA calls for an Operation Manipur to disarm illegal armed groups and scrap the SoO pact, while the state cabinet has approved the resumption of helicopter services to remote areas and COCOMI warns of intensified agitation from October 31. In Jammu and Kashmir, three people were arrested over an alleged assault on women and theft in South Kashmir and a security official reviewed the police’s operational readiness, while an attack on the Saudi Arabia airport in the region killed one Indian and injured two. A passenger bus in Chhattisgarh hit a roadside tree, killing six and injuring forty. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Manipur forblir ustabilt ettersom Kuki-Zo-kvinnergrupper og et forum krever presidentstyre, og en statlig MLA ber om en Operasjon Manipur for å avvæpne ulovlige væpnede grupper og avskaffe SoO-avtalen, mens statsrådet har godkjent gjenopptakelse av helikoptertjenester til avsidesliggende områder og COCOMI varsler intensivering av agitasjon fra 31. oktober. I Jammu og Kashmir ble tre personer arrestert for et påstått overgrep mot kvinner og tyveri i Sør-Kashmir, og en sikkerhetsoffiser gjennomgikk politiets operative beredskap, mens et angrep på Saudi-Arabias flyplass i regionen drepte en indisk og såret to. En passasjerbuss i Chhattisgarh traff et veikantetre, og seks personer ble drept og førti såret. 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
